rituals.name: SHAPE OVERLAY
rituals.plain:
Two shapes meet. Apparently shapes have chemistry.
Picture a circle and a triangle. Slide the triangle partly across the circle and hold the overlap. Notice the regions belonging only to the circle, only to the triangle, and to both.
Both original shapes remain visible.
Don't fuse the outlines into one new shape.

Don't try to make either stronger.

rituals.name: CAFÉ-WALL TILT

Reveal that the separator is straight only after the first impression.

rituals.name: AMBIGUOUS-FIGURE FLIP
rituals.plain:
One picture, two possible meanings. The first interpretation isn't royalty.
Construct a Necker cube: picture one square, then a second identical square slightly up-right, and connect matching corners. Keep the lines fixed while letting the nearer/front square flip once.
The drawn lines never change; only which face feels in front may switch.
Avoid redrawing the figure during the flip.

Return to the original detail set and ask which details don't actually change the root question.

Easy to read doesn't always mean true. Change the presentation.
Use 'Regular sleep supports attention.' First picture it in clear ordinary text; then picture the exact sentence in cramped faint lettering. Compare how immediately convincing or familiar it feels.
The sentence text is identical in both rounds.
Don't use readability as evidence for truth.
jolly.mindBend: An identical statement can feel more credible when it's easier to process.
jolly.safety: Use a small question about what matters for this pass. When forced positivity becomes noticeable, end the round; allow the difficult feeling.

rituals.name: PAPER-FOLD PUNCH
rituals.plain:
Fold, punch, unfold in imagination. Paper has some surprises.
Picture a square sheet folded in half, then in half again. Punch one mental hole away from the fold edges and unfold the sheet.
The punch passes through every folded layer.
Predict the full hole pattern before revealing it mentally.
